messages.author: 4024e1d3d6b890f6
messages.subject: floor_time() returns NA in fullseq_time()
parts:
There's a call to floor_time() in fullseq_time() that returns NA for
the first 5 seconds after each multiple of its time argument, and I
don't think it's the intended behaviour. It causes an error

Error in seq.int(0, to - from, by) : 'to' must be finite

In the call

seq.POSIXt(floor_time(range[1], time), ceiling_time(range[2],
time), by = time)

the arguments have the following values:

> range[1]
[1] "2010-08-09 00:05:01 IST"

> range[2]
[1] "2010-08-10 00:00:01 IST"

> time
[1] "5 hour"

The call ceiling_time(range[2], time) fails in its final line, which
is a call to floor_time().

Stepping through some calls to floor_time() I see the following return
values:

> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] "2010-08-10"
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:01", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] NA
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:02", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] NA
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:03", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] NA
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:04", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] NA
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 00:00:05", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] "2010-08-10"
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 05:00:04", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] NA
> floor_time(as.POSIXct("2010-08-10 05:00:05", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
[1] "2010-08-10 05:00:00"

Is this the intended behaviour?

Also, the help page for floor_time() says "Round date up to nearest
multiple of time" and ceiling_time() says "Round date down to nearest
multiple of time". Seems to be the other way round?

regards - David

>
> [1] "2010-08-10 05:00:00"

I believe that all the as.POSIXct calls above should by strptime
instead.

It is not, but the fault does not lie with ggplot2. The error is in
cut.POSIXt which floor_time uses.

cut(strptime("2010-08-10 00:00:01", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "5 hour")
# [1] <NA>
# Levels: 2010-08-10

I'm putting together a bug report for base R. For what it is worth,
the problem happens for specifications of time increments which are
more than one unit, and it happens for one less seconds after the
break. The started working again at 5 seconds was related to the
breaks being 5 hours. If it were 10 hours, it would be given NA for
the first 9 seconds after a break.

> Also, the help page for floor_time() says "Round date up to nearest
> multiple of time" and ceiling_time() says "Round date down to nearest
> multiple of time". Seems to be the other way round?

I'd think so. Hadley will have to fix that.

> regards - David
